newsitem.title: USA: First lady tours Little Rock tornado site.
newsitem.headline: First lady tours Little Rock tornado site.

text.p: First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton on Tuesday toured a mobile home park that was destroyed earlier this month by tornados and comforted a victim of the deadly storm.
Mrs. Clinton, with an entourage of about 75 people, appeared distressed as she looked over the rubble and stood near the place where three people died in the March 1 twister.
Shari Dunn, standing in front of the wreckage of what had once been her home, told Mrs. Clinton,"Can you look around? We have nothing. I'm grateful you've come because no one has been here."
"That's one reason I came today," the first lady said. She and President Bill Clinton lived for many years in Little Rock and consider it home.
Police said as many as 20 tornados swept through a 250-mile (400 km) swath of Arkansas on March 1, destroying hundreds of buildings and killing 25 people.

The trailer park in suburban Little Rock visited by Mrs. Clinton was one of the hardest-hit areas and still looked on Tuesday as if it had been hit by a bomb. Trees throughout the area were snapped in two and piles of twisted mobile homes lay all about.
Mrs. Clinton was accompanied to the site by Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee who earlier called the March 1 storm "apocalyptic."
Following her tour, Mrs. Clinton was to give a speech on literacy programmes for children and tour a new unit for infants a local hospital.
